shared_elements: low-relief carving on an upright, rounded/tapering slab
rows of small repeated sign-like marks in an upper zone
justification: Both surfaces show schematic low-relief human forms with disc motifs and small repeated sign-like marks arranged in an upper band on a tall stone slab with a tapering top, which is a loose but real correspondence in scheme. The decisive difference is that A is a single frontal anthropomorphic figure whose own body (arms folded to a chest disc, belt-like bands) is the whole composition, while B presents a multi-figure narrative in two stacked registers of figures facing one another across objects, a relationship type absent from A.
